text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- United Nations identifies ecstasy as main major drug problem in world at turn of century.
- Twelve families volunteer to look after juvenile offenders of children beyond parental control if court orders.
- Amcol Holdings ex-partner Roland Maurel finds potential buyers for abandoned U.S.$39.6 million joint-venture project in Mauritius.
- Printed circuit board maker Gul Technologies Singapore launch initial public offering of 30.15 million shares at Singapore 58 cents.
- Securities Commission Chairman Munir Majid says Malaysian stock market expects to move to shorter stock settlement by third quarter this year.
- Thailand's central bank orders 10 struggling finance groups to shore up reserves against bad loans.
- Singapore-based banks and investors with exposure in Thailand rattled by sudden halt in trading of banking and finance stocks.
- Thai baht down, but not out.
- Settlement period for Malaysian stock market will be cut to five trading days after transaction.
- Tuan Sing announces big jump in earnings, plans to redevelop flagship Robinson Towers into Singapore $200 million 35-storey tower.
- Keppel Telecommunications & Transportation announces a rights and warrants issue to raise up to S$124 million.
- Omni Industries' initial public offer of 54 million shares more than 130 times subscribed.
- Listed Osprey Maritime's group revenue rises 45 percent to U.S. $85.75 million for year ended December 31.
